questions.story:
On Learning an Instrument

Passage 1
There is no better use of a young person’s evening than an hour spent with a musical instrument. Music is not a hobby to be picked up when homework allows. It is a discipline, and every child who is denied it will grow into an adult poorer in every faculty that matters. Schools that treat music as an optional extra have simply not understood what they are dealing with.

Passage 2
The evidence is considerable. A 2019 study at the University of Helsinki followed one thousand two hundred pupils over six years and found that those receiving weekly instrumental tuition scored nineteen per cent higher in working memory tests than those who did not. A separate report by the National Foundation for Educational Research in 2021 recorded improved concentration in the same group across unrelated subjects.

Passage 3
Music teachers will also tell you that they can sense at once which children practise at home, and this impression is widely shared in the profession. Parents often remark that their children seem calmer after a lesson. It is worth adding that the violin in its modern form was developed in northern Italy during the sixteenth century, and that the instruments of that period are still admired for their varnish and their scroll work.

Passage 4
Against all this stands the lazy, corrosive fashion for letting children abandon an instrument the moment it becomes difficult. Every parent who permits this is teaching a child that effort is optional. Naturally, any thoughtful person already accepts that persistence must be taught young. Those who disagree have evidently not considered the matter seriously, for the case has always been perfectly plain.

questions.story:
Break, Break, Break
by Alfred, Lord Tennyson

Stanza 1
Break, break, break,
On thy cold gray stones, O Sea!
And I would that my tongue could utter
The thoughts that arise in me.

Stanza 2
O, well for the fisherman’s boy,
That he shouts with his sister at play!
O, well for the sailor lad,
That he sings in his boat on the bay!

Stanza 3
And the stately ships go on
To their haven under the hill;
But O for the touch of a vanish’d hand,
And the sound of a voice that is still!

Stanza 4
Break, break, break,
At the foot of thy crags, O Sea!
But the tender grace of a day that is dead
Will never come back to me.

Contextual, because the poem explains in a footnote exactly whose voice is meant
Conventional, because stillness always symbolises peace specifically
Contextual, because the phrase means only that somebody has stopped talking

questions.story:
Break, Break, Break
by Alfred, Lord Tennyson

Stanza 1
Break, break, break,
On thy cold gray stones, O Sea!
And I would that my tongue could utter
The thoughts that arise in me.

Stanza 2
O, well for the fisherman’s boy,
That he shouts with his sister at play!
O, well for the sailor lad,
That he sings in his boat on the bay!

Stanza 3
And the stately ships go on
To their haven under the hill;
But O for the touch of a vanish’d hand,
And the sound of a voice that is still!

Stanza 4
Break, break, break,
At the foot of thy crags, O Sea!
But the tender grace of a day that is dead
Will never come back to me.
questions.question: What contrast operates between the second stanza and the third?

options.text: The contrast between morning and evening on the same shore
The contrast between the sea and the land that borders it
The contrast between the living, who continue happily about their business, and the dead, who cannot be reached
The contrast between the fisherman’s boy and the sailor lad, who lead different lives

questions.question:
Consider these two observations from the poem:
Observation 1: The sea breaks in exactly the same way in the final stanza as it did in the first.
Observation 2: The speaker states that the tender grace of a day that is dead will never come back to him.
Which statement best expresses the theme built from these observations?

options.text: The sea is dangerous and should be treated with respect by those who live beside it
People should spend more time with their families while they still can
Grief is easier to bear when one is surrounded by happy children
The world continues unchanged by private grief, and what is lost to us is not returned
